why: grammar gap: A sloped trendline projected through the last two confirmed pivots (level = ph2Y + slope*(bar_index - ph2X), slope = (ph2Y-ph1Y)/(ph2X-ph1X)), plus the 'not yet broken' state per line. The grammar only has the last pivot as a flat level (pivot_high/pivot_low), not a line sloped through two pivots.

grammar gap: Arithmetic on prior-period OHLC for the breakout level. Pine's request.security(D, [high[1], low[1], close[1]]) feeds pivotPoint=(H+L+C)/3 and R1 = pivotPoint + 0.382*(H-L) (S1 = pivotPoint - 0.382*(H-L) for shorts). The grammar has prev_day_high and prev_day_low but no prev_day_close, and it cannot add, scale or combine terms. fib_pivot is a swing-pivot retracement, which is a different level.

grammar gap: Entry is a time-of-day rule (Pine hour/minute, enter only outside 08:30-11:58 once flat and 12 bars after the last exit) with no price or indicator condition. It sells a simulated CE/PE option strangle at strikes rounded to 200 points, which is direction-neutral. The grammar has no hour/minute clock filter, no bars-since-exit cooldown, and no option or strike legs.

grammar gap: Arithmetic on the current bar's own range: the entry needs min(open,close) >= high - 0.333*(high-low) for longs and max(open,close) <= low + 0.333*(high-low) for shorts (body inside the top or bottom third of the candle). The grammar has no way to scale one bar's high-low range, or to compare open/close against a fraction of that range.

grammar gap: Entry depends on wvf = (highest(close,22)-low)/highest(close,22)*100, then ta.stdev, ta.sma and ta.highest*0.85 percentile applied to that custom series (upperBand/rangeHigh), compared to its own prior-bar value. The grammar has no arithmetic between terms and no way to run an indicator on a derived series.

grammar gap: Calendar/time-based entry: the trigger is a lunar-cycle phase computed from the bar timestamp, (new + time + day*2) % cycle / cycle, with a crossover of 0.5 for New Moon and a wrap-around (diff < diff[1]) for Full Moon. The grammar has no bar-time or timestamp term and no modulo, so it cannot compute a 29.5-day cycle phase. valuewhen() on those events is also missing.

grammar gap: Pivot-sequence state kept in arrays (ArrayType/ArrayValue/ArrayIndex). The entry needs the last 5 classified swing points (HH/HL/LH/LL in a fixed order), then a retest of the stored level of the 4th-previous pivot (line.get_y1 of BeEntryLine/BuEntryLine) within an ELV*BeMove-bar validity window. The grammar only has the single latest pivot_high/pivot_low, with no Nth-previous pivot, no swing-type labels, and no stored price level to retest.

grammar gap: valuewhen() history of the last 5 alternating zigzag pivots (x, a, b, c, d) built from 5-bar fractals, with Fibonacci ratio tests between their legs (abc 0.382-0.886, bcd 1.13-2.618). The grammar only has the last confirmed pivot_high and pivot_low, with no earlier pivots and no arithmetic on price legs.

grammar gap: The entry needs the last five alternating zigzag pivots (valuewhen(zigzag, zigzag, 0..4)) and Fibonacci ratio tests between their distances, such as abs(b-c)/abs(a-b) in 0.382-0.886 and abs(c-d)/abs(b-c) in 1.13-2.618. The grammar has no pivot history beyond the latest confirmed pivot, no arithmetic or ratios between indicator values, and no way to alternate high and low pivots.

grammar gap: FRAMA (Fractal Adaptive Moving Average): an EMA whose alpha is computed from a fractal dimension built from log() of half-length and full-length high/low ranges on weekly security() data, with SC=200 and FC=1. The entry is a crossover of FRAMA against a second FRAMA applied to the first FRAMA's output. The grammar has no fractal-dimension adaptive MA and no way to feed one indicator's output into another.

grammar gap: The entry fires when output_signal turns up (output_signal > output_signal[1] and output_signal[1] <= output_signal[2]). output_signal is hma(avg(macd-signal diff/10, wpr(8), a Bollinger %B-style term, rsi(close - sma(close,21), 8), an RSI of DI difference, an RSI of a volume-weighted price ratio, an RSI of a smoothed stochastic term), 10)*2. The grammar cannot average several oscillators or apply hma/rsi to a derived series, so there is no honest single-indicator trigger.

grammar gap: Choppiness Index: 100*log10(sum(atr(1),n)/(highest-lowest))/log10(n), smoothed with sma(4). The entry fires when this index crosses to 61.8 or above on a rising close, or to 38.2 or below on a falling close. The grammar has no choppiness indicator, no log10, and no way to divide a sum of true range by the n-bar range. The Follow Trend filter also needs Parabolic SAR (sar), which is not in the grammar either.

grammar gap: No indicator-based entry trigger exists. The script replays hard-coded trades from a CSV text input (str.split/str.tonumber parsing, a map of Trade objects keyed by timestamp) and places strategy.order limit orders when time_close passes each CSV fill timestamp. Entries depend on calendar timestamps and user-supplied fill prices, not on any price or indicator condition.

grammar gap: Fisher Transform of the Hull MA: a recursive series (value := round_(.66*(normalized HMA - .5) + .67*value[1]); value1 := .5*log((1+value)/(1-value)) + .5*value1[1]) compared with its own previous bar and with the -5, 0 and +5 lines. The grammar has no Fisher transform and no way to build self-referencing smoothed series. The other entry conditions (CCI rising, HMA rising) are expressible, but they are only filters, so there is no honest entry trigger left once the Fisher is removed.

grammar gap: The entry trigger is crossover(mtfK, 50), where mtfK is linreg(request.security(higher timeframe, sma(stoch(close, high, low, 11), 3)), 11, 0). That is a higher-timeframe Stochastic with a linreg smoothing. The grammar has htf_close, htf_ema, htf_sma and htf_rsi but no higher-timeframe stochastic, no linreg term, and no way to apply an indicator to a higher-timeframe series. The short side has the same problem with crossunder(mtfD, 50).

grammar gap: Running cumulative sum of a per-bar series (Pine nRes = nz(nRes[1],1) - (open - close) + (xopenH1 - xcloseH1)), then sma() of that custom series. The grammar has no accumulator and no way to apply sma to a user-built series. The entry (sma(nRes,18) > nRes -> long, < -> short) depends on that series.

grammar gap: Entry depends on cumulative buy/sell volume delta (volume split by close position in the bar) summed since the bar of the highest-volume buyer/seller in the lookback, which then drives a remaining-power % and decay angle. It also needs a 5-segment high/low linear-regression channel for trend and zone classification. None of this is in the grammar: there is no cumulative delta since a ranked-volume event bar, no per-event remaining-power tracker and no regression channel. The strategy.entry code is also cut off in the pasted script.

grammar gap: highestbars()/lowestbars() (bars since the n-bar high/low), needed to build the Aroon Up/Down lines (length 8) whose crossover is the entry trigger. The grammar has no Aroon or bars-since-highest/lowest term.

grammar gap: Resting limit/stop entries at fixed absolute price levels (strategy.entry with limit=/stop= at grid_1..grid_10, derived from the user-input center_price and a step percent), laddered with pyramiding and per-level fill flags. The grammar has no input.price anchor or pending-order fills. The levels are asset-specific constants, so there is no indicator-based trigger to extract.

grammar gap: Calendar-based entry trigger: dayofmonth == month_day / dayofweek == week_day combined with ta.change(dayofweek). The grammar has no day-of-week or day-of-month term, and the script has no price or indicator condition to extract.

grammar gap: ta.ema() applied to a derived series: the entry line is an EMA of a fib level computed from ta.highest(high, N) and ta.lowest(low, N), i.e. EMA((highest-lowest)*(1-fib)+lowest, len). The grammar cannot do arithmetic on indicators and then smooth the result, and fib_pivot is pivot-based and unsmoothed. Without that line, the entry (low dips below it, close back above it) has no honest trigger.

grammar gap: ta.vwma applied to a user-built series: bull_vol/bear_vol (bar volume split by the candle's open/high/low position), then compared against each other with a flat-zone ratio filter (vol_flat / avg_vol < 1 - delta/100), and entry only on the first bar of the zone (the up == 1 / dn == 1 counter). The grammar has no volume-split series, no way to apply an average to a computed series, and no 'first bar of a state' counter.

grammar gap: Time-of-day entry trigger: hour(time, "America/New_York") == 2 and minute(time, "America/New_York") == 0. The script only enters on the 02:00 New York bar, and the grammar has no hour/minute-of-day condition. The remaining conditions (last break-of-structure direction and swing-trend direction) are persistent states that would fire on every bar without that clock gate.

grammar gap: Rolling percentage of the last 34 bars whose close sits in the top third (state 3) or bottom third (state 1) of the bar's high-low range, i.e. a loop counting state[i] values, then ema() of that count and a crossover between the two smoothed series. The grammar has no close-location-in-bar-range term, no bar-condition counting, and no way to apply an EMA to a derived series.

grammar gap: Dynamic support 'base' levels: the script loops over the prior 100 bars, counts how many min(close,open) values lie within 0.5% of the current one, and stores those clustered price levels in a Pine array (array.unshift/array.sort). It then takes the nearest base below price as the level that close crossed under within 5 bars, and enters when close is 2% below that level. The grammar has no touch-count clustering and no arrays of price levels, and pivot_low/lowest are different things.

grammar gap: linebreak(tickerid, src, nl) - the Line Break (three-line-break) synthetic chart type. The entry is the colour of its lines (lb_o < lb_c). Those lines form only when close breaks the prior N lines' range, and the colour persists between breaks. The grammar has no way to build this series.

grammar gap: request.security on external QUANDL CFTC Commitments of Traders data (non-commercial long/short positions, weekly). The entry depends on an external fundamental data series that is not price, volume or any indicator in the grammar.

grammar gap: Both entry triggers need features outside the grammar. (1) `crossover(zx,0)` depends on an RSI of `cum(change(T_c)*volume)`, which is a cumulative volume-weighted series, smoothed by a WMA and an EMA of its lagged difference. (2) `crossover(linear_reg, b)` needs `linreg(close,25,0)`, the linear regression endpoint, crossing a higher-timeframe Hull-style average built from `wma` calls on `close[1]` with a shift. The grammar has no `linreg` and no RSI of a custom series.

grammar gap: Parabolic SAR (Pine sar(0.02,0.02,0.2) / ta.sar) and its close-crossover trigger. The grammar has no acceleration-factor stop-and-reverse indicator, and Supertrend is ATR-based, so it would not be the same signal.

grammar gap: Parabolic SAR (Pine sar(start, increment, maximum)): an accelerating-factor trailing reversal level. The entry is a stop order at the SAR price, which fires when price crosses the SAR. The grammar has no SAR term, and the ATR-based supertrend is a different calculation.

grammar gap: Arithmetic combining several indicators into a new series. The entry compares a 21-bar average of (ta.stoch * ta.rsi / (close/close[9]*100)) with its own previous value (avr > avr[1]). The grammar has no way to multiply or divide indicators, or to average a derived series.

grammar gap: Indicator-on-indicator input: the entry is a flip of an ATR trailing stop (HMA-smoothed range x4) computed on an RMA(22)-smoothed Bollinger %B series (length 100, stdev 10) of open, high, low and close. The grammar's supertrend only runs on price bars, so it cannot be applied to a derived oscillator series.

grammar gap: COT.requestCommitmentOfTraders (CFTC Commitment of Traders positioning data) feeds the netIndex extreme filter that gates the default entries, and there is no COT series in the grammar. The Stochastic Momentum Index (SMI_smoothed crossing -40 / +40) is also not a grammar indicator.

grammar gap: Time-of-day entry trigger: the script enters only on the 01:00 New York bar (Pine hour/minute, (hour-5)%24 == 1 and minute == 0). It also uses a var state that stores the colour of the candle before the 00:00 bar and reads it an hour later. The grammar has no hour-of-day or minute condition and no value latched at a specific clock time.

grammar gap: Entry fires when total_score (a sum of about 12 weighted sub-scores) crosses a threshold. The sub-scores are Bollinger-step count, stepped RSI, volume-delta streaks, prior-day/week volume-profile value area, absorption, stochastic, CCI, normalized MACD, ADX, pivot/round-number key levels, and RSI/SMT divergence. The sum is then rescaled by EMA-slope, SMMA-distance and ADX multipliers and compared with a threshold that switches on close vs EMA200. The grammar has no arithmetic on indicators, no weighted score accumulation, no volume profile, and no stateful streak counters, so there is no single honest trigger to extract.

grammar gap: The entry fires on a turn in `pred`, a custom series built from `lsq()` (correlation(x,y,p)*stdev(y,p)/stdev(x,p) regression of `gendata` on `sec`), then passed through the nested-EMA `karo()` transform. `gendata` includes `random(i) = second(time) * close[i]`, which reads the seconds field of the bar timestamp. The grammar has no rolling correlation or regression series, no timestamp-seconds input, and no way to apply a user-defined transform to another series and then detect a local minimum or maximum (pred[1]<pred[2] and pred[1]<pred).

grammar gap: Calendar month/date conditions (Pine `month`, `year`, and `time("W")`/`time(res)` new-period detection). The entry fires on the first bar of a user-selected calendar month, and the grammar has no month-of-year or date term.

grammar gap: Calendar/day-of-week trigger (Pine dayofweek(time) == N, or a bar_index-based every-X-bars counter with var state). The entry is a fixed date/schedule DCA buy with no price, indicator or volume condition, and the grammar has no day-of-week, timestamp or bar-counter term.

grammar gap: No term for the script's custom bull_score/bear_score (a linearly weighted, true-range-weighted close-location sum over 50 bars). No term for the adaptive upper_zone/lower_zone, which is the mean ± 1.75 stdev of the last 30 stored bull/bear crossover levels (array.push/array.avg/array.stdev over event history). The entry fires on bull_score crossing bear_score outside that zone, or on bull_score sitting above upper_zone.
grammar gap: math.random() - the entry fires on a random draw (r == random_signal), which is not a function of price or volume, and the grammar has no random or noise term

grammar gap: Day-of-week condition (Pine `dayofweek == 4`, which is actually Wednesday, not Friday) and the backtest date-range filter `time >= start and time <= end`. The grammar has no calendar day-of-week or timestamp term, and nothing else in the script triggers the entry.

grammar gap: Portfolio-state tracking: entry fires when the simulated portfolio's holdings drift from a target allocation (var-tracked coin quantities and balance across bars, plus request.security of other symbols). There is no price-based trigger, and the grammar has no portfolio value or allocation-drift term.

grammar gap: request.security()/security() on other symbols (Quandl CFTC COT net-positioning series and the weekly auxiliary ticker EMAs) - the entry requires external-symbol data, which the grammar cannot read. The only expressible leg, ema(4) rising, is not the script's trigger on its own.

grammar gap: Dynamic parent-session levels. The script keeps arrays of the high/low of each killzone session (Asia, London and New York, defined in America/New_York time). It picks as 'parent' the earlier session whose range fully contains the next session's range, then enters when price sweeps that parent's high/low and later closes back inside it. The grammar has only fixed-hour UTC range_high/range_low windows. It has no way to select a parent range by nesting, carry that level forward until it is swept, or wait an arbitrary number of bars for the reclaim.

grammar gap: Elder Force Index: ta.rma(ta.change(close) * volume, n) (efi with n=15 and n=120). The entry needs efi2 > 0, efi < 0 and efi rising. The grammar has no way to build a moving average of close-change times volume, and no volume-weighted momentum oscillator to stand in for it.

grammar gap: No absolute candle-body size term and no arithmetic between series. The entry needs math.abs(close - open) compared with 4 times the 20-bar average of that body. body_pct is body as a share of the bar's range, not the size of the body against recent bodies, so it cannot stand in for the trigger.

grammar gap: ta.mfi (Money Flow Index, volume-weighted RSI-style oscillator) is not in the indicator list, so the entry trigger (SMA of MFI rising two bars in a row, with close above SMA 200) cannot be built
grammar gap: No entry logic to translate: the script body contains only strategy("My Script") with no indicators, conditions, or strategy.entry calls. Please paste the full Pine source.

grammar gap: User-defined recursive adaptive filter: `trend := trend[1] + gain * ((src - trend[1]) + 0.25 * flow_push)`. The gain is a sigmoid of summed z-scores (`ta.sma`/`ta.stdev` of order-flow `dlp`, `liquidity_density`, and the second difference of realized volatility of log returns). The entry `close < trend and proj > trend` (short: `close > trend and proj < trend`) compares price to this custom `var` series, and the grammar has no custom series, z-score arithmetic, log returns or stateful recursion. No grammar indicator (ema, kama, etc.) reproduces it faithfully.

grammar gap: Parabolic SAR (ta.sar with start/increment/maximum acceleration factor), including the daily higher-timeframe version via request.security(ta.sar(...)). The grammar has no SAR indicator. Supertrend is a different ATR-band trailing line, so using it would be a silent wrong translation.

grammar gap: No entry trigger exists: long_condition and short_condition are hardcoded to false, so the script never enters. It is a template whose only logic is session filters, a fixed-percent/ATR stop, and direction/date inputs.

grammar gap: Custom composite series built from a rolling per-bar count of candle-pattern flags (doji, spinning top, shooting star, hanging man, marubozu, hammer, bullish and bearish engulfing, three white soldiers), averaged into one oscillator. The grammar has no way to define a boolean pattern series, sum it over n bars, or combine the results arithmetically. The long and short entries are ta.crossover(averageOscillator, 0.1) and ta.crossover(averageOscillator, 0.2), so there is no other trigger to extract. The var score accumulators are never reset each bar, so the script's own oscillator is also a cumulative sum rather than a true 14-bar window.
grammar gap: The script contains only strategy("SMA", overlay=true) and has no entry condition, no strategy.entry call and no indicator logic, so there is no trigger to extract.

grammar gap: Session-anchored open price and clock-time gating. The entry compares the close at 30 minutes after the 09:30 America/New_York session start with that session's opening price (ny_open_for_bias := open on new_sess, then window_close_px > or < it). It then enters once per session on the bar after that window. The grammar has no open-of-a-clock-time-session reference, no DST-aware New York timezone, and no once-per-session or after-window-bar gating. htf_open only reads the open of a completed higher bar, not the current session's open.

grammar gap: request.security() of CFTC COT data (cot.COTTickerid via the LibraryCOT import), with Williams %R computed on that external series rather than on price. The grammar has no external or non-price data feed, so the %R trigger has nothing to read.

grammar gap: Calendar and time-of-day conditions: dayofmonth() and dayofweek() in the Asia/Tokyo timezone (gotobi days, i.e. day of month divisible by 5, plus the Friday-before-weekend rule) and time() session windows (0200-0955 and 0955-1500 JST). The grammar has no day-of-month, day-of-week or intraday session-hour filter; range_high/range_low only read a UTC window's high/low and cannot gate entries by clock time or date.

grammar gap: The entry trigger is `bool(entrySource)`, where `entrySource` is a user-chosen `input.source` (default `close`, which is always true). The script defines no signal of its own. It also places a martingale grid of limit orders (`strategy.entry` with a limit price, scaled sizes) instead of one entry.
grammar gap: random() - the entry trigger is a random number draw (enter_frequency > random(0,100)) with no market-data condition, and the grammar has no random or probabilistic term

grammar gap: request.security("SMH", timeframe.period, close/open) - the entry needs another symbol's candle (SMH close > SMH open), and the grammar only has the chart symbol's own data and higher-timeframe data of that same symbol

grammar gap: request.security() on a second symbol (AMEX:URTH) to build the spread series ((close - globalIndex)/globalIndex*100), then ta.rsi() applied to that spread. The grammar has no other-symbol data and RSI only runs on the chart's own close.

grammar gap: Relative Volatility Index: the script splits stdev(close,10) into up and down series by close vs close[1], smooths each with a Wilder 13/14 recursion (nU, nD), computes 100*nU/(nU+nD), then takes an EMA of that. The grammar cannot feed a custom series into an indicator, and has no RVI. The entry is the state nRes > 50 (long) or nRes < 50 (short), which cannot be built from stdev, rsi or ema alone.
